title: Route PDFs, Office files and images to the right parser in /v1/scrape (Content-Type plus magic bytes)
summary: After any driver returns bytes, sniff Content-Type and then the first bytes (%PDF-, a zip containing [Content_Types].xml, OLE compound file, PNG/JPEG/WebP). If the body is not HTML, hand the already-fetched bytes to the matching parser in quarry-transform (pdf.rs, docx.rs, images.rs) instead of running charset decoding and readability over binary data, and record the detected kind in output metadata. Express it as a typed Replan::IsFile when the planner work in R-t2-03-06 lands.
whyItMatters: PDFs and Office files linked from sites are a common knowledge-base input. Today a PDF URL goes through readability and produces garbage markdown that users notice immediately, even though a PDF text extractor already exists.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (firecrawl), unique; table-stakes for a Firecrawl-class scraper
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: kind = sniff(content_type) or sniff_magic(first 512 bytes): %PDF-, PK zip with [Content_Types].xml, OLE compound file, PNG/JPEG/WebP. If kind is not html, raise AddFeature(pdf|document|image) carrying the already-downloaded bytes as prefetch so the parser needs no refetch. Record kind in output metadata.

verevonToday.gap: Scrape has no file-type routing. PDF extraction is used only by the answer pipeline; DOCX and image parsers exist but nothing calls them.

approach: Ingestion Plane: add a sniff_kind(content_type, bytes) helper after the driver fetch in quarry-runtime/src/pipeline.rs and dispatch to quarry-transform pdf/docx/images, with size caps and artifact offload for large files. For browser fetches that land on a download, reuse the bytes the browser downloaded. Set the output metadata content kind and a typed skip reason for unsupported types. Later fold into the Replan vocabulary (R-t2-03-06) and the planned /v1/parse route.
risks: Large or malicious files: enforce byte caps, parser timeouts and sandboxing; decompression bombs in zip-based Office files.

verevon.exactGap: PageRunner reads Content-Type only for the PageFetched event and charset decode, then runs readability on every body (pipeline.rs:440-506), so a PDF or Office URL produces garbage markdown. The needed pieces already exist elsewhere: answer.rs has is_pdf (Content-Type or %PDF- within the first 1 KiB, answer.rs:683-753) and calls pdf::extract_text (answer.rs:839, 25 MB cap in pdf.rs:40/203), docx::extract_text exists with a 25 MB cap but has no non-test callers, and images.rs is not an image parser (HTML lazy-image/srcset helpers only), so the item's PNG/JPEG/WebP leg has no parser to route to.

verevon.constraints: Ingestion Plane only; no cross-plane dependency. Keep byte caps (pipeline 16 MB, PDF and DOCX 25 MB), parser timeouts and zip decompression-bomb limits since DOCX is a zip. Under ZDR extracted text stays inline with no artifact write. Changing output for non-HTML bodies changes fingerprints used by change monitors, so record the detected content kind in metadata.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reuse the existing is_pdf sniffer instead of writing a new one and add the zip-with-[Content_Types].xml check for Office files; route PDF and DOCX only. Remove images.rs as the image target: it cannot parse image binaries. Image bodies need OCR or a vision call, which is a separate and larger item, or a typed unsupported_media skip reason for now. Legacy OLE .doc should be a typed skip.
verevon.effortNote: S holds for PDF plus DOCX routing because sniff and both parsers exist; image/OCR routing is out of scope and would be M.
verevon.verdictReason: The scrape pipeline really lacks file-type routing, but PDF sniffing and extraction already ship in the answer path, DOCX is written but unwired, and the image parser the item names does not exist; reword to PDF and DOCX reuse.

reference.corrections: The OOXML/ODF check sniffs only the PK 03 04 local-file header and excludes genuine ZIP media types. It does not look for [Content_Types].xml. The first-512-bytes window is a recommendation: the reference computes HANDOFF_SNIFF_BYTES from its signature table. The order is: a GCS PDF reference first, then the Content-Type header, then magic bytes. Image routing is not always on: it needs a deployment switch (IMAGE_OCR_ENABLED plus a FirePDF base URL) and the per-request parsers option. Otherwise images are rejected as unsupported files. Archives, audio, video and executables are rejected explicitly. The rest of the mechanism, including the prefetch handoff so parsers do not re-download, is accurate.
caveats: Image OCR handoff is deployment-gated and option-gated; PDF parsing quality depends on the FirePDF service, which is external in the hosted product
Apify Website Content Crawler selects files by content type but only downloads them and does not parse them (DOC), so '1 of 4' holds for parser routing
